name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.NonUnitalCStarRepresentation.exists_nonzero_projection_scalar_corner
title: A nonzero projection with scalar corner

content.display_title: A nonzero projection with scalar corner
content.one_sentence_role: Constructs a projection in the original algebra from an isolated non-scalar character of a unitization subalgebra.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed. Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ be a nonzero irreducible representation representing the unique unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible representations of $A$. There is $p\in A$ with $$p^*=p=p^2,\qquad p\ne0,\qquad \forall a\in A\ \exists c\in\mathbb C:\ pap=cp.$$
content.assumptions: Separability is imposed on $H$. The algebra need not be unital or separable. The scalar $c$ may depend on $a$, while the projection $p$ is fixed.
content.conclusion: The same nonzero star projection has a one-dimensional algebraic corner $pAp=\mathbb Cp$.
content.proof_summary: Find an isolated character away from the scalar character, take its characteristic-function projection, show that its scalar coordinate vanishes, and extend its scalar corner from the abelian subalgebra to the ambient algebra.
proof_steps: Write $\widetilde A=\mathbb C\oplus A$, $\iota(a)=(0,a)$, and $\chi_\infty(\lambda,a)=\lambda$. Choose $a_0\ne0$ in $A$ and put $b=a_0^*a_0\ne0$. In the unitization $\widetilde A$, its image $\iota(b)$ is self-adjoint. Apply [Maximal abelian containment](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/MaximalAbelianContaining.lean#L53-L59) to obtain a maximal abelian unital $*$-subalgebra $D$ containing $\iota(b)$. It is closed and commutative. The character countability theorem [Countability of this character space](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/CharacterCountable.lean#L93-L114) applies to the given singleton $\pi$, separable $H$, and this closed $D$.

The element $\iota(b)\in D$ is nonzero and has scalar coordinate zero. Together with countability, these are the inputs to [An isolated non-scalar character](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/MinimalProjection.lean#L34-L75), yielding an isolated character $\chi\ne\chi_\infty|_D$. Its singleton is both open and closed in the character space. Thus the continuous function $1_{\{\chi\}}$ corresponds under the Gelfand transform to a nonzero projection $q\in D$ satisfying $$qd=\chi(d)q\qquad(d\in D),$$ by [The projection of an isolated character](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/IsolatedCharacter.lean#L22-L70).

That characteristic function is zero at the different character $\chi_\infty|_D$, so $\chi_\infty(q)=0$. This value is precisely the scalar coordinate of $q\in\widetilde A$. Therefore $q=\iota(p)$ for an element $p\in A$. Injectivity of $\iota$ transfers $q^*=q=q^2$ and $q\ne0$ to $p^*=p=p^2\ne0$.

The ambient corner calculation is [From maximal abelianness to a scalar ambient corner](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/MinimalProjection.lean#L22-L66). For any $z\in\widetilde A$, put $x=qzq$. Since $D$ is commutative and $qd=dq=\chi(d)q$, for $d\in D$ we get $$xd=qzqd=\chi(d)x=dqzq=dx.$$ Maximal abelianness therefore puts $x$ in $D$. Apply the earlier equation to this $x$: $qx=\chi(x)q$. But $q^2=q$ makes $qx=x$, so $qzq=\chi(x)q$.

Finally set $z=\iota(a)$ for an arbitrary $a\in A$. With $q=\iota(p)$, the last equation is $\iota(pap)=\iota(cp)$ for $c=\chi(q\iota(a)q)$. Injectivity of $\iota$ gives $pap=cp$. This proves the universal scalar-corner condition on the same $p$.
